issue_context.title: Sonos is leaking memory over time
issue_context.body:
### The problem

`2021-04-01 19:05:25 CRITICAL (SyncWorker_0) [homeassistant.components.profiler] Memory Growth: [('Subscription', 536, 4), ('_ProcessSonosEventQueue', 536, 4), ('Thread', 609, 3)]`

`_ProcessSonosEventQueue` keeps growing in memory.



### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

dev

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

n/a

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

sonos

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

Turn on `start_log_objects` https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/profiler/#service-profilerstart_log_objects 

Then watch the log
comments:
Potential fix:
```
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/sonos/media_player.py b/homeassistant/components/sonos/media_player.py
index 5e59918650..04c07d973f 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/sonos/media_player.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/sonos/media_player.py
@@ -589,6 +589,10 @@ class SonosEntity(MediaPlayerEntity):
 
             player = self.soco
 
+            # If already subscribed, do not do it again
+            if self._subscriptions:
+                return
+
             def subscribe(sonos_service, action):
                 """Add a subscription to a pysonos service."""
                 queue = _ProcessSonosEventQueue(action)
```
Verified this change works and solves the memory leak and ip change still works as expected

review_comments: If we prefix a function name with `async_` it should mean that we should call the function from inside the event loop.
Resolved in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/48684 (but docker hub is broken at the moment so the CI is likely to fail)
We should use `self.hass.async_add_executor_job` to schedule on the executor.
This is being called back from `pysonos` which can only take a callback so we can't `await` here.

But it doesn't need to be awaited because that's all add job does under the hood anyways.  Will adjust.

Surprisingly makes more sense when not looking at it after midnight and getting sleep 🤦‍♂️
Resolved in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/48684 (but docker hub is broken at the moment so the CI is likely to fail)
We shouldn't use `hass.async_add_job` if we know what the target is.
